prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: But we will also need to balance these adjustments with various considerations related to, e.g., our commercial strategy and our broader position in a nonideal environment.
DEMAND: we will also need to balance these adjustments with various considerations related to, e.g., our commercial strategy and our broader position in a nonideal environment
BEARER: we (Anthropic)

cli.result:
1. We (Anthropic) are required to weigh these adjustments against various considerations. Two examples of these considerations are those related to our commercial strategy and, separately, those related to our broader position in a nonideal environment. The list is not complete, so other considerations may also have to be weighed.
2. We (Anthropic) are required to weigh these adjustments against various considerations, including those related to our commercial strategy and our broader position. Here "in a nonideal environment" applies to both: both the strategy and the position are to be considered as they stand in a nonideal environment. Again, the list is not complete.
